entries.title: Tamil at a glance
body: Tamil is a Dravidian language with about 85 million speakers, official in Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka and Singapore. Its literature goes back over two thousand years, to the Sangam poems, and it was the first language to be declared a classical language of India.

Tamil builds words by adding suffixes in a fixed order. The verb comes last and agrees with the subject, including its gender and politeness. There is a wide gap between the formal written language and everyday speech.

entries.title: How Tamil script works
body: Tamil script has 12 vowels and 18 consonants, plus the special letter ஃ (aaytham). Each consonant carries a short a, and the other vowels are marks around it, giving 216 combined letters. The dot above (புள்ளி) removes the vowel: க் is k alone.
Tamil has fewer letters than other Indian scripts because one letter covers several sounds: க is k, g or h depending on where it falls in the word.

entries.title: The letter ழ
entries.body: ழ is a sound few languages have: an r-like approximant made with the tongue curled far back, written zh in transliteration. It is in the name of the language itself, தமிழ் (thamizh). Tamil also distinguishes three l sounds (ல, ள, ழ), two r sounds (ர, ற) and three n sounds (ந, ன, ண).

entries.title: The present tense
entries.body: Stem + -கிற்- + a person ending. The endings are the same in the past (-த்- / -ன்-) and future (-வ்- / -ப்-) with a different tense marker.

entries.title: Case endings
entries.body: Endings join the noun. Nouns in -ம் change it to -த்து- or -த்- before most of them: மரம் → மரத்தில்.

entries.title: Numbers
entries.body: Tamil has its own numerals (௧ ௨ ௩ …) but they are rarely used today; everyday writing uses 0–9.

entries.title: Pongal
entries.body: Pongal is the Tamil harvest festival in mid-January. Rice is boiled with milk and jaggery in a new pot until it bubbles over, while people call out “பொங்கலோ பொங்கல்!” The overflowing pot stands for plenty in the coming year, and the third day honours the cattle that work the fields.
